summary: The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate failed on input validity: the custom experiment has an empty floorplan and empty power_w, but a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object. input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass are both false, simulation_allowed is false, and comparison_valid is false. The extraction also records no independent verification, and the adversarial methods, code, parameters, config and data checks and the page/asset review are unresolved. The selected scenario is the Figure 9b CMO layout (alpha = 0.5) of a 12-chiplet multi-window display system on a 2.5-D passive silicon interposer. The paper reports a HotSpot 7.0 temperature of 373.58 K, described as a system-level maximum in Section 4 but as an average in the abstract, against 381.41 K for the initial layout. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so any result would be a steady-state snapshot with no transient trace. The paper has no workload time series or controller, so a one-row power trace would not be paper-derived. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace source commit applies. No source commit is available and no paper-linked artifacts were found. No generated placement or input.flp/input.ptrace was produced, so no placement assumption can be reported beyond the fact that Figure 9b coordinates are image-only and any placement would be illustrative. No Studio temperature exists, so no numerical comparison with 373.58 K is made, and no replication is claimed. Qualitatively, the paper reports that temperature-aware placement lowers the peak by about 8.34 K while cutting communication energy from 1026.72 uJ to 794.59 uJ. That sensitivity concerns the optimizer, which Studio does not model. Numerical comparison would require matching location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions. The mismatches are: 2.5-D interposer/TSV/bump/FR-4 stack versus simplified 2D; fin-channel forced-air heatsink with spreader and TIM versus an unspecified Studio boundary; a different solver from HotSpot 7.0; unpublished layer parameters; an ambiguous peak-vs-average aggregation; an unstated steady/transient mode; and non-numeric layout coordinates.
limitations: Studio did not run because the custom experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w; the verdict is the screening label only, with no thermal result.
comparison_valid is false, and no numerical comparison with 373.58 K or 381.41 K is made or implied; exact replication is not claimed.
The paper's observable is ambiguous: Section 4 says maximum temperature while the abstract says average, and the hotspot location is not stated.
The paper does not state whether HotSpot was run in steady-state or transient mode, and a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace.
Numeric x/y coordinates for Figure 9b are unavailable, so any placement would be an illustrative construction rather than the paper's layout.
The Table 2 name-to-power mapping is ambiguous in the extraction, and total power is not published, so no per-chiplet power inputs were established.

Essential physical mismatches remain: 2.5-D silicon interposer with TSVs, microbumps, C4 bumps and FR-4 versus a 2D model; forced-air fin heatsink, spreader and TIM versus Studio boundary conditions; and HotSpot 7.0 versus a different solver.
The CMO communication-energy optimizer is outside Studio's scope, so the 794.59 uJ and 1026.72 uJ values are not thermal observables and cannot be reproduced.
No paper-linked code or data was found, no source commit is pinned, and Studio package and material assumptions were not supplied.
Several verification checks (adversarial methods, code, parameters, config, data, and page/asset review) are unresolved, and the evidence is not independently verified.

The paper models a 2.5-D stack with a passive silicon interposer, TSVs, microbumps, C4 bumps and an organic FR-4 substrate. A simplified 2D steady-state runner cannot reproduce this vertical conduction path, so its temperatures would not be physically equivalent.

The cooling in the paper is a fin-channel forced-air heatsink (fan radius 10 cm, 5000 rpm, lateral airflow, 30 mm fins) plus a spreader and TIM. A simplified Studio boundary condition cannot be assumed to match this.

The paper's optimizer (CMO heuristic with a communication-energy objective) is not part of the Studio thermal runner. Only the thermal evaluation of a given placement can be approximated, not the optimization itself.
The final chiplet coordinates of Figure 9b are published only as an image and not as numeric x/y values. Any Studio placement would be an illustrative construction, not the paper's layout.
The solver differs: the paper uses HotSpot 7.0 with its own layer, material and bump parameters, most of which are not listed. A different solver cannot be compared numerically with 373.58 K.

The paper has no transient workload or controller, and no reliability analysis beyond a mention of judging reliability from temperature. A one-row power trace is therefore not a paper-derived time series.

The paper assumes uniform power per chiplet and a chiplet surface temperature equal to the overall temperature. It also uses theoretical sizes (actual size plus spacing grid) for placement. These conventions may differ from a Studio geometry.

The paper-derived facts are the Table 2 chiplet dimensions and powers (PDF page 5), the HotSpot settings, and the 373.58 K peak value. Any coordinates produced by the runner are separate illustrative 2D placement values, not paper-derived.
Total chip power is not split by any rule. Only the per-chiplet powers in Table 2 are used, and dimensions and powers come from the same MWD scenario.
If dimensions and powers alone are used, the runner builds a separate illustrative 2D placement and a one-row (constant) power trace.

The Studio package, material and cooling assumptions are not specified in the supplied packet and must be recorded from the bundled Studio configuration. They should not be presumed to equal the paper's silicon interposer, TIM and forced-air heatsink stack.
Studio temperatures are not compared numerically to the paper's 373.58 K and do not claim exact replication.
